messages.subject: Re: xlsx speed
messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,

No changes were made to slow things down intentionally.  I certainly don't notice it with my setup.  I've sent your question to the list, in case somebody else has encountered the same problem.

Try different versions/OS just to make sure you can clearly isolate the issue.

Adrian

Smaller tables (~100 rows X ~8 columns) now take 5 minutes or more to write.  Larger tables (~1000 rows x 10 columns) fail with a Java heap space error message. messages.subject: Re: xlsx speed
messages.body_plain:
Are you sure that the newer version is the only thing that has
changed? Is it possible that your template has  changed too? It could
be something dumb like you changed the format of a whole row or a
column; now, instead of reading a few non-empty cells, R has to read a
whole column which can take a very long time. (theory not tested.)

messages.subject: Newbie question regarding alternate date format input from Excel
messages.subject_clean: Newbie question regarding alternate date format input from Excel
messages.body_plain:
I am new to R (as you can probably guess) and I am trying to import some simple data from Excel:

1]  myDate   datapoint1  datapoint2...
2]  07/2012      1.0             1.5   ...
3]  08/2012      1.4             6.9
.
.
.

So essentially month/year.  Using read.xlsx directly interprets myDate as a factor.  I can use read.xlsx2 and specify the colClasses as "Date"

mydataframe2 <- read.xlsx2(workbook2, 1, colClasses=c("Date",rep("numeric",5)))

read.xlsx2 correctly reads in the data type as "Date" but read.xlsx2 doesn't recognize the month/year formatting:

> str(mydataframe2)
'data.frame':   24 obs. of  6 variables:
 $ myDate        : Date, format: NA NA NA NA ...
 $ All.Patients: num  15.62 6.6 4.29 8.96 3.53 ...
 $ n13under    : num  7.41 0 0 7.38 4.76 ...
 $ n14over     : num  26.19 11.48 7.69 11.39 2.33 ...
 $ n15under    : num  6.56 0 0 6.67 4.17 ...
 $ n16over     : num  31.4 14.6 10.3 13.6 2.7 ...

Any suggestions how I can read in the month/year data with the xlsx package?

The month/year column in the .xls spreadsheet is formatted as a Date.

messages.subject: Reading Month/Year data
messages.body_plain:
I am new to R (as you can probably guess) and I am trying to import some simple data from Excel:

1]  myDate   datapoint1  datapoint2...
2]  07/2012      1.0             1.5   ...
3]  08/2012      1.4             6.9
.
.
.

So essentially month/year.  Using read.xlsx directly interprets myDate as a factor.  I can use read.xlsx2 and specify the colClasses as "Date"

mydataframe2 <- read.xlsx2(workbook2, 1, colClasses=c("Date",rep("numeric",5)))

Read.xlsx2 then correctly recognizes the data as "date" data, but can't seem to parse the month/year formatting:

> str(mydataframe2)
'data.frame':   24 obs. of  6 variables:
 $ Date        : Date, format: NA NA NA NA ...
 $ All.Patients: num  15.62 6.6 4.29 8.96 3.53 ...
 $ n13under    : num  7.41 0 0 7.38 4.76 ...
 $ n14over     : num  26.19 11.48 7.69 11.39 2.33 ...
 $ n15under    : num  6.56 0 0 6.67 4.17 ...
 $ n16over     : num  31.4 14.6 10.3 13.6 2.7 ...

The first column of data is formatted as date (not character) in the Excel spreadsheet.

Any suggestions how I can read in the non-standard format month/year data with the xlsx package?

Thank you!

Sam

messages.subject: Re: Reading Month/Year data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sam,

As I replied to you in private, you need to figure out if your "Date" column is a Text or a Date in Excel?  I guess it's Text. If you get a factor, you can always convert a factor to a character using as.character().  For read.xlsx2, the column class should be "character" for the first one, not a Date.

If using read.xlsx, you'll need to construct from the string "07/2012" a Date.  Something like:
  mydataframe2$month <- as.Date(paste("01/", mydataframe2$Date, sep=""), format="%d/%m/%Y")

Best,
Adrian
